videos.script: After VirtualBox, the hypervisor you are most likely to find on a desktop is VMware Workstation. It is older, polished, and for years it was the one companies paid for. {{workstation}} Its terms have changed a lot lately. The free little brother, Player, has been retired, and Workstation itself became free. So you will meet both: new installs of Workstation, and old copies of Player that still work. {{licences}} This computer cannot run VMware, so this lesson does the parts that are not VMware's alone. Its disk format, which every hypervisor reads. And the package that carries a whole machine from one hypervisor to another. {{portable}} Then the names you need on the phone. Three networks called VMnet0, VMnet1 and VMnet8. A file ending in vmx. And VMware Tools. {{names}}
